summary: Full-repository Round 1 security review of iFocus (commit fb078be) verified zero keystroke/frame persistence and zero third-party dependencies, but identified 3 P1, 4 P2, and 1 P3 confirmed vulnerabilities across lock-screen camera/AX gating, modal/auth window occlusion, hardBlocklist enforcement, shared /tmp build/signing paths, PID-reuse cache poisoning, SecureFileStore directory validation, and coordinator log memory bounds.

findings.title: Webcam and AX tracking reactivate while locked on screen-wake or spoofed DistributedNotification
findings.rationale: Ambient lock-screen wake events (notifications, lid open, desk bump) or any unprivileged local process posting to DistributedNotificationCenter control `activateNames` events (`screensDidWakeNotification`, `didWakeNotification`, `com.apple.screenIsUnlocked`). `SystemSessionStateProvider` initializes `activeLock = true` without querying WindowServer and unconditionally calls `setActive(true)` on any `activateNames` notification instead of checking `CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary()` (`kCGSessionOnConsoleKey` and `CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), while `AppController.runCalibrateCommand()` never observes session lock/sleep at all. Crossing the locked-console and unauthenticated IPC boundary into TCC-privileged Camera/Accessibility causes `AppController` to restart `AVCaptureSession` (720p webcam capture) and AX polling while the Mac screen is still locked, or lets any local process spoof `com.apple.screenIsLocked` to silently disable iFocus.
findings.suggestion: Track display/system sleep booleans separately from lock/console state, query `CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary()` on init, on every workspace/distributed notification, and inside `isSessionActive()` to require `(dict[kCGSessionOnConsoleKey as String] as? Bool ?? true) && !(dict["CGSSessionScreenIsLocked"] as? Bool ?? false)` before marking active, and observe `SystemSessionStateProvider` in `AppController.runCalibrateCommand()` so sleep/lock stops the camera during CLI calibration.

findings.title: CGWindowCatalogService drops layer != 0 windows, blinding hit-testing to modal and auth dialogs
findings.rationale: Modal alerts (`kCGModalPanelWindowLevel`), system authentication/TCC prompts (`SecurityAgent`, `CoreAuthUI`, `UserNotificationCenter`), floating panels (`kCGFloatingWindowLevel`), and popup menus render at `kCGWindowLayer > 0` above normal `layer == 0` terminal windows. `WindowHitTester` relies on non-eligible front windows in `snapshot.windows` returning `.blocked`, but `CGWindowCatalogService.snapshot()` discards all entries where `layer != 0`, making foreground dialogs and overlays completely invisible to occlusion checks even under default settings (`requireAllowedSource = true`). Looking at a Touch ID/TCC dialog, password-manager overlay, or menu positioned over a background terminal crosses the foreground UI modal boundary and raises/focuses the underlying terminal after 0.30-0.45s, dismissing menus or diverting subsequent keystrokes/passphrases into the shell.
findings.evidence:
for entry in rawList {
    guard let layer = (entry[kCGWindowLayer] as? NSNumber)?.intValue, layer == 0 else { continue }
findings.suggestion: Add `layer: Int = 0` to `WindowDescriptor` and require `window.layer == 0` in `WindowHitTester.isEligible(_:config:)`, retain visible windows with `0 <= layer && layer <= Int(CGWindowLevelForKey(.screenSaverWindow))` (filtering out own PID, status-bar items with `layer >= 24 && bounds.height <= 36`, and non-interactive system chrome like `com.apple.WindowManager` / `com.apple.dock`) so `layer > 0` dialogs act as `.blocked` occluders, and veto switching globally whenever an on-screen window from `SecurityAgent`, `com.apple.LocalAuthentication.UIAgent`, `com.apple.UserNotificationCenter`, or `com.apple.coreservices.uiagent` is present.

findings.title: SafetyPolicy skips Config.hardBlocklist when requireAllowedSource is false and omits CoreAuthUI
findings.rationale: When a system security dialog (`SecurityAgent`, `CoreAuthUI`, `UserNotificationCenter`, `System Settings`) becomes frontmost while a user has configured `requireAllowedSource: false` (a documented setting for gazing from browsers/IDEs into terminals), `SafetyContext.frontmostBundleID` identifies the privileged prompt. `DefaultSafetyGuardPolicy.evaluate(_:)` checks `isBundleAllowed(context.frontmostBundleID)`—the sole call site enforcing `Config.hardBlocklist` on the active source app—only when `requireAllowedSource == true`, and `Config.hardBlocklist` also omits `com.apple.LocalAuthentication.UIAgent`, `com.apple.UserNotificationCenter`, `com.apple.ScreenSharing`, and `com.apple.Settings`. Gaze landing on a visible terminal crosses the system authentication focus boundary and steals keyboard focus from the security prompt, routing subsequent password or Return keystrokes into a terminal shell.
findings.suggestion: Check `if let front = context.frontmostBundleID, Config.hardBlocklist.contains(front) { return .deny(.sourceNotAllowed) }` unconditionally before the `requireAllowedSource` check in `DefaultSafetyGuardPolicy.evaluate(_:)`, and add `"com.apple.LocalAuthentication.UIAgent"`, `"com.apple.UserNotificationCenter"`, `"com.apple.ScreenSharing"`, and `"com.apple.Settings"` to `Config.hardBlocklist`.

findings.title: Build and app-signing scripts execute and sign binaries from predictable shared /tmp directories
findings.rationale: Any co-tenant local user or compromised low-privilege service account on macOS has write access to sticky `/tmp` and can pre-create `/tmp/ifocus-sbx` (or `/tmp/ifocus-build`, `/tmp/clang-cache`, `/tmp/swiftpm-cache`, `/tmp/swift-modcache` in `scripts/bundle-app.sh:17-26`) with permissive mode or as a symlink. `scripts/sbx.sh` runs `mkdir -p "$OUT"` without `mktemp -d`, symlink rejection, UID ownership checks (`-O`), or `0700` mode enforcement, then writes `Runner.swift`, compiles `ifocus` and `tests`, executes `"$OUT/tests"`, and feeds `$OUT_DIR/ifocus` into `codesign` in `scripts/bundle-app.sh`. Crossing the shared `/tmp` boundary into developer execution and `codesign` allows local arbitrary code execution during `./scripts/sbx.sh test` or signing an attacker-replaced Mach-O binary into TCC-privileged `dist/iFocus.app`.
findings.suggestion: Default `IFOCUS_SBX_OUT` (and `--swiftpm` cache/scratch paths in `scripts/bundle-app.sh`) to UID-scoped paths such as `/tmp/ifocus-sbx-$(id -u)` (or `mktemp -d /tmp/ifocus-sbx.XXXXXX`), and validate every scratch/cache directory with a helper that creates missing directories with `mkdir -m 0700`, aborts if `[ -L "$dir" ]` or `[ ! -O "$dir" ]`, and enforces `chmod 0700 "$dir"` before compiling, executing, or signing.

findings.title: Uninvalidated PID-keyed bundleIDCache misclassifies windows after macOS PID wraparound
findings.rationale: Over multi-day menu-bar uptime on macOS (`PID_MAX = 99999`), a newly launched non-allowlisted or blocklisted process can receive a PID previously used by an exited allowlisted terminal. `CGWindowCatalogService.bundleIDCache` keys solely on `Int32` PID, returns cached bundle IDs before consulting `NSRunningApplication(processIdentifier:)`, and never evicts terminated PIDs or checks `launchDate`. Crossing the `Config.allowedBundleIDs` / `Config.hardBlocklist` eligibility boundary causes `WindowHitTester` to treat an untrusted process's window as an allowlisted terminal (allowing AX focus switches into it and failing to block occluded terminals behind it) while growing `bundleIDCache` without bound.
findings.suggestion: Replace the persistent `bundleIDCache` with a per-`snapshot()` local dictionary `var snapshotBundles: [Int32: String?] = [:]` (at most one `NSRunningApplication(processIdentifier:)` lookup per active on-screen PID every 200 ms), or key cached entries by `(pid, app.launchDate)` and prune exited PIDs.

findings.title: SecureFileStore.read accepts group/world-writable config directories and uses path-based TOCTOU
findings.rationale: On a shared Mac where `~/Library/Application Support/iFocus` (or a custom `directoryURL`) has group- or world-writable permissions (`0o775` / `0o777`), a co-tenant user controls directory entries (`unlink`, `link` hardlink to an older `0o600` user-owned file, or symlink swap). `SecureFileStore.read(_:)` calls `validateDirectoryStat(..., fixPermissions: false)`, which checks `(perms & 0o077) != 0` only when `fixPermissions == true` and silently accepts writable directories on read, while `read`/`write` re-resolve pathname strings across `lstat`, `chmod`, `open`, and `rename` instead of pinning a directory fd. Crossing the persistent config/calibration trust boundary allows silent deletion of `config.json` (resetting hardened settings to defaults) or hardlink rollback/TOCTOU substitution.
findings.suggestion: Throw `SecureFileStoreError.insecureDirectory` in `validateDirectoryStat` when `(perms & 0o022) != 0` (or `(perms & 0o077) != 0`) and `fixPermissions == false`, and open the directory once via `open(dirPath, O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC)` to perform `fstat`, `fchmod`, `openat`, `renameat`, and `unlinkat` relative to that descriptor.

findings.title: FocusCoordinator appends unbounded DecisionLogEntry records at 20-30 Hz, leaking heap memory
findings.rationale: During normal menu-bar operation, `AVCaptureVideoDataOutput` drives `FocusCoordinator.processSingleEvent(_:)` continuously at 20-30 Hz. Every processed event appends a `DecisionLogEntry` (retaining `WindowDescriptor` and `bundleID` strings on switches and mismatch alerts) to `private var decisionLog: [DecisionLogEntry]` with no ring-buffer bound, capacity limit, or eviction on `stop()`, even though `AppController` never reads `coordinator.log()`. Crossing the continuous sensor-stream resource boundary accumulates up to 108,000 entries/hour (~2.6M/day at 30 fps), causing monotonic heap growth and eventual memory exhaustion/termination of the safety coordinator.
findings.evidence:
private var decisionLog: [DecisionLogEntry] = []
...
decisionLog.append(DecisionLogEntry(
    timestamp: now,
    action: .none,
    veto: output.veto,
    candidateWindowID: output.candidateWindowID,
    outcome: nil
))
findings.suggestion: Cap `decisionLog` as a bounded ring buffer (e.g., `maxLogEntries: Int = 4096`, which exceeds `deskThree` 60s test runs of 1,201 steps while bounding memory to < 512 KiB) or make decision logging opt-in for test/simulation callers.

findings.title: Cancelling or failing interactive calibration silently clears user pause state and starts camera
findings.rationale: When a user explicitly pauses iFocus for privacy (`isPaused == true`, camera off) and then opens `Calibrate...` from the status menu before pressing `Esc` (`.failure(.cancelled)`) or hitting a capture error, `AppController.runInteractiveCalibration()` controls the post-calibration state transition. Line 279 overwrites `isPaused` with `true` without recording the prior pause state, and lines 321-322 unconditionally execute `await coordinator.setPaused(false)` and `await startTrackingIfReady()`. Failing open across the user's explicit privacy-pause boundary silently restarts live webcam streaming and AX focus switching after a cancelled or failed calibration.
findings.evidence:
await coordinator.setPaused(true)
await coordinator.stop()
...
case .failure(.cancelled):
    break
case .failure(let err):
    warningBanner = err.description
}

await coordinator.setPaused(false)
await startTrackingIfReady()
findings.suggestion: Capture `let wasPaused = await coordinator.paused()` before calling `await coordinator.setPaused(true)` in `runInteractiveCalibration()`, and restore `await coordinator.setPaused(wasPaused)` on `.failure(.cancelled)` and `.failure(_)` (calling `startTrackingIfReady()` only when `!wasPaused`, or restoring `wasPaused` across all exit paths).
